observations.header_and_grouping: Four model columns follow category and benchmark stubs. Eight category groups make a long comparison scannable; category labels are bold and sometimes wrap.
observations.alignment_and_precision: Labels are left aligned and values centered. Precision is inconsistent within some rows: integers appear beside one-decimal scores.
observations.emphasis_and_color: Caption defines bold highest and underlined second. One row displays two identical 44.6 scores but assigns different emphasis, leaving rounded-tie treatment ambiguous.
observations.rules_and_spacing: Only horizontal category rules, with no vertical grid. The table is narrower than the text block despite a measured body under seven points.
observations.caption_and_footnotes: Caption below identifies slow-thinking evaluation and the emphasis policy; model versions remain in headers.
observations.missing_values_and_uncertainty: No missing outcomes or intervals in the selected table. No explicit tie tolerance.
observations.scientific_comparability: Models differ in size and mode implementation. The table is a reported benchmark comparison, not a matched-resource ablation.

measurement_caveats: Text sizes are nominal extracted PDF values in points for the selected table body, not whole-page fonts.
Stroke counts include underlines and separators; long-horizontal objects are separately retained, and filled black hairlines are not background shading.
Baseline gaps are candidate separations between extracted numeric text baselines, not a guarantee of row-height semantics.
The table crop includes its caption; the measurement rectangle isolates its body.
RGB convenience values are extracted and quantized; opacity 1.0 denotes opaque rendering, not an inferred low-alpha source color.

lessons: Use category stubs and section rules for long benchmark lists.
Require a declared rounding and tie policy before styling winners.
cautions: Do not copy differing ranks for equal displayed values without explaining hidden precision.
Do not adopt unnecessary downscaling as a design default.
